hypothesis: Corrections lane: the catalogue sits >2 px (200 m) from the DEM-curvature scarp crest / magnetic-gradient ridge along a consistent direction, so dots should be emitted on the evidence-defined trace rather than on the (masked) catalogue line.
mechanism: A real registration error shows as (a) a signed offset mode away from zero that exceeds the random null, and (b) crest-steered dots recovering hidden mapped faults better than evidence-free dots in the same corridor.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Erosional terraces and alluvial-fan edges give the same convex break-in-slope with no fault; 1:50,000-1:1,000,000 map generalisation and 100 m rasterisation displace a line by 1-3 px with no fault involved. Both are why the random-offset null and the evidence-free corridor null exist in E2/E3.

result_E1_MEASURED.reading: offsets cluster UNDER two pixels (median 1.48 px), the signed median is -0.11 px (no preferred side), and the distribution is barely separated from the random null (0.326 vs 0.273 beyond 2 px). The brief's stop rule for crest steering is met.

holdout_dti.evaluator_version: h57-hide-and-recover-v1 (src/metrics.py, alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, 300 m triangular kernel, visible faults masked pixel-exactly)
holdout_dti.label: HOLDOUT-DTI (never an organizer score)

E2_spatial_folds.caveat: IR-57-001: whole-component spatial withholding puts the hidden faults far from every visible trace, so a corridor-restricted emitter structurally cannot reach them. This mode measures that fact; it cannot test the corrections claim.

E3_neighbour_strand_folds.reading: crest steering is WORSE than the evidence-free corridor at the identical dot budget (0.00087 vs 0.00177, paired CI strictly below 0, P(beats)=0.0). The crest-steering component of the hypothesis is REFUTED on real withheld mapped faults.
